remaining_blockers.title: Production enterprise readiness gaps
remaining_blockers.detail: Egress sandbox (network firewall around codex/claude shells), per-caller MCP auth (bearer tokens / OAuth on MCP transport), signed Docker images (cosign), SLSA provenance attestation, SBOM generation. These are not in scope for RC; they belong to a R4+ Enterprise Hardening round.

remaining_high_risks: A2A DNS rebinding: 2 documented residuals — egress-proxy SSRF (mitigation at firewall layer) + kernel BGP/anycast hijack (mitigation at RPKI/mTLS layer). Both out of scope for pure-Python HTTP adapter.
MCP guardrail: audit log at default path is world-writable; no per-caller auth — defense-in-depth gap for multi-tenant MCP deployment.
WorkerIsolator cleanup TOCTOU: shutil.rmtree is non-atomic — accepted residual; fd-pinning out of scope.
Docker image: no runtime attestation, no rootless guarantee, no SBOM. Image works but not enterprise-grade by SLSA standards.
next_round_recommendation: Round 4 — Enterprise Hardening: (1) SLSA provenance via cosign + sigstore on Docker images; (2) SBOM generation in release.yml; (3) per-caller MCP auth (bearer or OAuth); (4) egress-sandbox documentation for codex/claude shell execution; (5) PyPI publish + Homebrew formula sha256 update after PyPI live; (6) WorkerIsolator fd-pin alternative for atomic cleanup.
